transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

I keep getting up from my station or popping up during meetings when I’m supposed to stay put. It’s like I take off before I even think about it. My supervisor says it’s becoming a safety problem at work, so… that’s why I came in.
Did you have similar trouble sitting still or feeling restless when you were a child?
Yeah. Even in elementary school, I couldn’t stay in my seat. I’d wander around the room, talk over the teacher, blurt things out. I got a lot of notes sent home about it.
Aside from being restless, do you also struggle with keeping your focus or attention on tasks?

Yeah. With inventory logs or the CNC training pages, I’ll start out trying to focus, but after a few minutes the numbers or words kind of blur together. Then I have to go back because I realize I didn’t take any of it in.

latest_inference.note: Patient confirms prominent inattention symptoms in addition to hyperactivity and impulsivity spanning from childhood to adulthood, ruling out predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation (F90.1) and confirming ADHD, combined type (F90.2).

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of motor hyperactivity, inability to remain seated, and impulsivity suggests ADHD (hyperactive/combined types), with differentials including mania/hypomania in bipolar disorder, anxiety-related psychomotor agitation, or restless legs syndrome/akathisia.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, combined presentation, exhibiting persistent symptoms of both inattention (difficulty sustaining focus, poor comprehension/retention during work tasks) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (inability to remain seated, blurting out, motor restlessness). Symptoms have been present since childhood and cause clinically significant functional impairment in the workplace.
